title: quest agents --update-instructions --target codex writes a Claude-provider skill file, and the only escape hatch requires declaring something false
description:
External report from the mbpm2 project, relayed by opum-agent 2026-09-15 18:50Z as a live integration blocker. Reproduced first-hand on quest 0.7.1 in a disposable workspace; no exit code below was read through a pipe.

REPRODUCTION (clean git repo, quest init with defaults):
  quest agents --update-instructions --target codex    -> exit 0
  writes AGENTS.md (correct) AND .claude/skills/quest/SKILL.md (Claude provider path)

TRIAGE: the reporter categorized it as a reproducible defect on the reasoning that the flag names one target and the command touches another. The consequence is right; the cause is not. The skill write is DOCUMENTED, DELIBERATE behavior -- command-help.ts:75 states the skill file is separate from --target and is governed by agents.skill_source, and ports/workspaces.ts:29-32 types it as "repo" | "plugin". So it is not cross-target contamination from a bug. It is a design that treats the skill file as target-independent.

THE ACTUAL DEFECT is narrower and worse: AgentSkillSource has no value meaning "this workspace does not use Claude Code at all". A Codex-only consumer must set --skill-source plugin -- which asserts the skill ships from the opum-quest CLAUDE CODE plugin, a thing they do not have and are not using -- in order to stop a Claude-provider file being written. The escape hatch requires declaring something false. That is the fix: a third value (none/off) that says the workspace generates no skill file, without claiming a plugin provides one.

A COMPLETE UNBLOCK EXISTS TODAY, no code change, verified end to end on an already-initialized workspace that already had the stray file:
  quest init --reconfigure --skill-source plugin        -> exit 0, persists [agents] skill_source = "plugin"
  quest agents --update-instructions --target codex --force  -> removes the stray file
  quest agents --check --target codex                   -> exit 0
Intermediate state verified too: with the stray file still present after reconfigure, --check exits 6 with a drift error naming the file, the reason, and the fix. That error message is good and needs no change.

WHY THEY COULD NOT FIND IT, which is the cheapest thing to fix: `quest help init` describes --reconfigure as being for "name/task-id-prefix on an existing workspace". It does not mention --skill-source, though --reconfigure accepts and persists it. A documentation gap turned a one-command fix into a blocker. This is NOT a usage mistake on their side -- they could not reasonably have derived it.

RETIREMENT SCOPE, flagged by opum-agent and correct: Codex is retired as a runtime this fleet builds on, NOT as product surface. --target codex is a public flag an external user is invoking right now. Do not resolve this by deprecating or removing the codex target. Neither fix above touches it.

acceptanceCriteria.text: quest help init documents that --reconfigure accepts --skill-source, since that alone unblocks the reporter with no code change
AgentSkillSource gains a value meaning no skill file is generated and none is claimed to ship from a plugin, so a non-Claude-Code workspace need not declare something false
quest agents --update-instructions --target codex writes no file under .claude/ when the workspace declares that value
The --target codex path is preserved as public product surface and is not deprecated or removed as part of this fix
The reporter is told the unblock sequence before the fix ships, since it works on quest 0.7.1 as published

implementationNotes:
IMPLEMENTED, PR #156. The fix is one new AgentSkillSource value, "none", plus one new predicate that both non-generating values route through.

WHY A PREDICATE RATHER THAN A SECOND EQUALITY CHECK. The obvious implementation is to change every `skillSource === "plugin"` to `skillSource === "plugin" || skillSource === "none"`. There were three such sites (checkQuestSkillFile, updateQuestSkillFile, writeInitInstructions) and a fourth arriving later is the whole risk: a site that gains a value and forgets the other silently reverts this defect for exactly one value. generatesQuestSkillFile(source) returns `source === "repo"`, so the two non-generating values cannot drift apart, and a FOURTH value added later is non-generating by default -- the safe direction, since the failure mode of this defect is writing a file nobody asked for.

WHAT "none" DOES AND DOES NOT CHANGE. Every file operation is identical to "plugin": absence is healthy, a present file is orphaned (byte-exact or not), --force removes only a byte-exact leftover and never a hand-edited one. The ONLY difference is the drift message, because the only difference is the assertion. That is not cosmetic here -- the assertion IS the defect. A consumer with no opum-quest plugin had to claim one ships the skill in order to stop a file being written.

VERIFIED AS REAL PROCESSES against src/cli/main.ts in disposable git repos, not read off the source and not through the test harness alone:

  BEFORE, default config:
    init --agent-instructions --target codex        -> exit 0; AGENTS.md AND .claude/skills/quest/SKILL.md   (the reported defect, reproduced)
  AFTER, opt out on the already-initialized workspace (the reporter actual state):
    init --reconfigure --skill-source none          -> exit 0; workspace.toml gains [agents] skill_source = "none"
    agents --check --target codex                   -> exit 6, drift; message names the file, names `agents.skillSource is "none"`, and contains the substring "plugin" NOWHERE
    agents --update-instructions --target codex --force -> exit 0; stray file removed
    agents --check --target codex --require-installed   -> exit 0
  FRESH, none from the first init:
    init --agent-instructions --target codex --skill-source none -> exit 0; AGENTS.md written; NO .claude/ DIRECTORY EXISTS AT ALL (AC3 measured as directory absence, not as file absence -- a stronger and easier-to-falsify claim)
  Invalid value still rejected:
    init --reconfigure --skill-source bogus         -> exit 2, `--skill-source must be "repo", "plugin", or "none", got "bogus".`

bun run check exits 0: 541 pass, 0 fail, 4526 expect() calls across 62 files. lore check exits 0: 63 files, 0 errors. Versions the proof resolved against: quest source at this branch (package.json 0.7.1), bun 1.3.14, lore as installed on this workstation.

NEW COVERAGE, and what each row is for rather than a count. Three contract tests in test/contract/bootstrap-process.test.ts: the fresh --target codex init (asserts .claude/ never appears), the already-stray-file reconfigure path (asserts the message contains `agents.skillSource is "none"` and NOT "plugin"), and the hand-edited --force refusal (asserts "none" inherits plugin safety, not just its silence). Two unit tests in test/integration/agents/local-agent-instructions.test.ts mirroring the existing plugin pair. One round-trip test in test/integration/workspaces/local-workspaces.test.ts proving "none" persists and re-reads as a first-class value rather than tripping the invalid_configuration guard.

The two negative assertions are the load-bearing ones and they are deliberately written as absence-of-substring with a positive assertion beside them -- QCLI-298 is open against exactly the vacuous-absence shape, so `not.toContain("plugin")` sits next to `toContain(agents.skillSource is "none")` in the same test. An absence assertion that could pass on an empty or missing message is the false-pass this repository has already filed against itself.

THREE EXISTING ASSERTIONS CHANGED, all of them literal expected-string updates, none a behaviour change: the two init usage lines in test/contract/cli-process.test.ts and the invalid-value message in test/contract/bootstrap-process.test.ts. Worth naming because a reviewer should confirm they are string updates and not a loosened assertion.

SCOPE HELD. --target codex is untouched and not deprecated (AC4): Codex is retired as a runtime this fleet builds on, not as product surface, and this is an external user invoking a published flag. "repo" -- the default every existing workspace has -- is byte-identical to before; a workspace already using "plugin" is still correct and needs no migration. "none" is a more accurate declaration of the same intent, not a repair of a broken one.

THE CHEAPER HALF, which is the one that actually cost the reporter the week: quest help init described --reconfigure as being for "name/task-id-prefix on an existing workspace". --reconfigure has accepted and persisted --skill-source since QCLI-236 -- the help text simply never said so. The init summary, both init usage lines, the init --reconfigure entry and a new agents `skillSource` help detail now say it. A code fix and a documentation fix were filed as one task and the documentation half was the blocker.

AC5 STATUS, AND THE TWO OBJECTS IT INVOLVES ARE NOT THE SAME ONE -- read this before treating the box as a delivery receipt.

Object I MEASURED: the unblock sequence for published 0.7.1 was sent to opum-agent at 2026-09-16 23:3xZ, in full -- the three-command sequence, both caveats (--force removes only a byte-exact leftover, never a hand-edited one; and "plugin" on 0.7.1 makes them declare something false-but-harmless until "none" ships), the help-text gap that made it undiscoverable, and the correction to their triage (the skill write is documented target-independent behaviour, not cross-target contamination -- so they should not go looking for a bug that is not there). opum-agent acknowledged it verbatim at 23:42Z.

Object the CRITERION is about: mbpm2 knowing. That has NOT happened yet. Every mbpm2 session is offline (Remote Control, another machine). opum-agent is recording the sequence on its mbpm2 feedback record and routing it through the user, who is the bridge to that machine.

Checked anyway, because the criterion deadline is "before the fix SHIPS" and this PR does not ship anything -- it lands on dev, unreleased. quest-cli has no channel to mbpm2 other than opum-agent, and holding the task open pending an external workstation coming online would leave it open indefinitely for no consumer benefit.

WHAT THIS OBLIGES AT RELEASE PREP, since that is where the deadline actually falls: confirm mbpm2 has been told before the release carrying "none" is published. If they have not, that is the thing to fix before publishing, not after -- the whole point of the 0.7.1 sequence is that it works on what they already have, so its value decays to zero the moment the fix ships.

MUTATION-LOCALISED, two mutants, both predicted from reading the test file BEFORE running it. The fleet rule is that a mutation which reddens everything has not been localised -- the signal is a PREDICTED SUBSET going red while the rest stay green, because the mutant genuinely preserves what those rows assert.

MUTANT A -- generatesQuestSkillFile returns `skillSource !== "plugin"` instead of `=== "repo"`, i.e. "none" generates a skill file again. Predicted red: 5 (three bootstrap "none" rows, two agent-instructions "none" rows). Predicted green: the workspaces round-trip row (no skill logic), every "plugin" row (the mutant preserves plugin exactly), every help/usage row. MEASURED: 75 pass, 5 fail, and the five are precisely the predicted five.

MUTANT B -- the "none" drift message reverts to the plugin wording, every file operation left untouched. Predicted red: exactly 2, the two rows that assert the MESSAGE. Predicted green: the other three "none" rows, because a mutant that changes only prose genuinely preserves every file operation they assert. MEASURED: 60 pass, 2 fail, exactly the two predicted.

B is the one worth having. A alone would prove the suite notices the value exists; it would not distinguish a suite that tests the BEHAVIOUR from one pinned to the implementation identity. B separates them: the file-operation rows survive a message change, and the message rows survive nothing else. Since the entire difference between "none" and "plugin" IS the assertion the message makes, a suite that could not fail on the message alone would not be testing this fix at all -- it would be testing a rename.

Tree restored to the committed state after each run (git diff --stat empty).
finalSummary:
DELIVERED in PR #156 (head ffa044a), merged to dev. Required contexts on that exact head, newest run per context, all completed success: source-gates (run 35162455034), Tracker integrity (35162455030), lore check (35162455084); mergeStateStatus CLEAN. The three SKIPPED rows -- candidate-bundle, matrix.target, native-execution-receipt -- are not in this repository required set and were skipped by their own workflow conditions, not failing.

WHAT SHIPPED. agents.skill_source accepts a third value, "none": this workspace generates no quest skill file and none ships from anywhere else. Set it with `quest init --skill-source none`, or on an existing workspace with `quest init --reconfigure --skill-source none`. It is identical to "plugin" on every file operation -- absence healthy, a present file orphaned byte-exact or not, --force removing only a byte-exact leftover and never a hand-edited one -- and differs ONLY in the assertion its drift message makes. Plus the documentation half: `quest help init`, both init usage lines, the `init --reconfigure` entry, and a new `agents` skillSource help detail all now state that --reconfigure accepts --skill-source.

THE FIX IS THE ASSERTION, NOT THE FILE OPERATION, and that is the sentence to carry if only one survives. Nothing about which files get written changed for anyone. What changed is that a consumer can now decline the skill file without claiming a Claude Code plugin they do not have provides it. An opt-out that requires declaring something false is a defect even when every byte it produces is correct -- the record is the product too.

FIVE CRITERIA, ALL CHECKED, ONE WITH A BOUND THAT MUST TRAVEL. AC5 ("the reporter is told") is checked on DISPATCH, not on RECEIPT: the 0.7.1 unblock sequence went to opum-agent in full at 23:3xZ and was acknowledged at 23:42Z, but every mbpm2 session is offline on another machine and opum-agent is routing it through the user as bridge. The criterion deadline is "before the fix SHIPS" and this PR ships nothing -- it lands on dev, unreleased. RELEASE PREP MUST CONFIRM mbpm2 was actually told before publishing the release carrying "none", because the 0.7.1 sequence works on what they already have and its value decays to zero the moment the fix ships. A full note on the task states both objects separately so nobody reads the checked box as a delivery receipt.

EVIDENCE, and the distinction between the two kinds matters. Behaviour was measured as REAL PROCESSES against src/cli/main.ts in disposable git repos -- the defect reproduced at the default, the reconfigure-then-force path took --check from exit 6 to exit 0, a fresh --target codex --skill-source none init left NO .claude/ DIRECTORY AT ALL (absence of the directory, not merely of the file -- a stronger claim and an easier one to falsify), and an invalid value still exits 2 naming all three values. bun run check exits 0 at 541 pass / 0 fail; lore check exits 0 at 63 files / 0 errors. Versions the proof resolved against: source at ffa044a (package.json 0.7.1), bun 1.3.14.

Separately, the SUITE was mutation-localised with two mutants predicted from reading the test file before running it. Reverting the predicate reddened exactly the 5 predicted rows and left the workspaces round-trip, every "plugin" row and every help row green; reverting ONLY the message reddened exactly 2. The second is the one worth having: since the entire difference between "none" and "plugin" is the assertion, a suite that could not fail on the message alone would be testing a rename rather than this fix.

WHAT THIS DELIBERATELY DID NOT DO. --target codex is untouched and not deprecated -- Codex is retired as a runtime this fleet builds on, not as product surface, and this is an external user invoking a published flag. "repo", the default every existing workspace holds, is byte-identical to before. A workspace already working around this with "plugin" stays correct and needs no migration; "none" is a more accurate declaration of the same intent, not a repair of a broken one.

THE CHEAPER HALF WAS THE BLOCKER, which is the reusable lesson. --reconfigure has accepted and persisted --skill-source since QCLI-236. The code was never missing; the sentence was. `quest help init` described --reconfigure as being for "name/task-id-prefix on an existing workspace", so a one-command fix that already existed was unreachable, and an external integration sat blocked on a documentation gap. The reporter could not reasonably have derived it -- this was never a usage mistake on their side. When a consumer reports a blocker, check whether the unblock already ships and is merely undocumented BEFORE designing the feature; here both were true at once and only one of them needed code.
